note: The full requirement set for this project, one row per requirement, in the brief's own order. Three disciplines are enforced by tools/validate_decisions.py rather than trusted: (1) every row carries at least one source id that resolves in ledger/sources.json, (2) a row whose status is PARTIAL or NOT_MET must name the evidence showing why, and a row whose status is MET must name where the implementation lives, so a status can never be asserted without a pointer, (3) no row may state a result that contradicts the register: a PARTIAL row must carry a gap, and a MET row must not. Status vocabulary is closed: MET, PARTIAL, NOT_MET, UNVERIFIABLE. UNVERIFIABLE is used only where the brief asks for something no official source defines, and such rows must say what would make them checkable.

status_vocabulary.MET: An implementation exists in this repository and the row names it.
status_vocabulary.PARTIAL: Part of it exists; the row names what is missing.
status_vocabulary.NOT_MET: Nothing in this repository attempts it.
status_vocabulary.UNVERIFIABLE: The brief asks for this, but no official source defines the target or the measurement, so it cannot be established as met or unmet. The row names what would make it checkable.

groups.name: Programme and compliance requirements
groups.lead: What Amazon's own published terms require of this Site. These are not preferences; a violation is a material breach under S01 §2 and §6.

rows.requirement: The Site must clearly and prominently state "As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases."
rows.evidence: Rendered by every generator: tools/build_site.py::DISCLOSURE (footer of all 37 pages/), marketing/scripts and tools/build_marketing.py (9 pages), and the static footer of the root pages. tools/validate_data.py::check_disclosure and tools/audit_site.py::check_disclosure fail the build when the sentence is absent from any published page.

rows.requirement: A link-level disclosure must sit next to the affiliate link itself, because US FTC guidance requires the disclosure to be hard to miss and placed with the endorsement message rather than only on an about page.
rows.evidence: The three product articles each carry an in-context `(paid link)` marker inside the CTA block (marketing/articles/p1.html, p2.html, p3.html each contain 1; content/templates/product_article.md.tmpl line 60 renders it), and tools/validate_data.py fails a page that has class="sponsored-link" without class="disclosure--link".
rows.gap: Measured 2026-11-15 across marketing/: 7 pages carry an outbound amazon.com/dp/ affiliate anchor (27 anchors in total) but only 3 of them carry an in-context marker. The four without one are marketing/articles/index.html (3 anchors), marketing/comparison.html (6), marketing/flagged.html (3) and marketing/verification.html (3). Each of those carries the page-level disclosure strip, which is why the existing gate passes, but not the label next to the link that S11 asks for.

rows.requirement: The Site must not display a product price except in a link or widget served by Amazon, and must not run price-tracking or price-alerting functionality.
rows.evidence: No page in this repository prints a product price. The rule is executable, not aspirational: tools/validate_data.py::check_no_product_prices and the CI step "No page prints a price and every page discloses" fail on a dollar figure inside a buying context. The price-tracking prohibition is carried as compliance rule R-22 and wired to module M-03.

rows.requirement: The Site must contain original content and be publicly available at the address supplied in the application.
rows.evidence: The site is public at https://kanlerxz87-cyber.github.io/Zone2/ (GitHub Pages, verified via the Pages API in earlier sessions and in this session's deploy check). It is original in the sense that every value is transcribed and attributed rather than copied.
rows.gap: Amazon's own published bar for the content itself is not yet met on its face: S38 states all Sites must have "robust original content (even when advertising is removed)" with "at least 10 posts", and that website content must be recent, "generally within the last 60 days". The published article set is 3 product articles plus 1 buying guide and 1 comparison (marketing/routes), and no page carries a byline or an author. Whether 5 editorial pages satisfy "at least 10 posts" is a judgement Amazon makes, not this repository; the count is recorded here so the gap is visible rather than assumed away.

rows.requirement: Special Links must use the assigned Associates ID and the tagged link format Amazon provides, and must not be cloaked, hidden or spoofed.
rows.evidence: The compliance rule set covers it (ledger/compliance.json R-07, R-08, R-24) and tools/link_builder.py builds tagged URLs from a configured Associates tag.
rows.gap: No Associates ID is configured for this project, so no published link is monetized: the marketing pages render "preview link — no Associates ID configured, earns nothing". The three supplied link.amazon URLs also resolved without a tag parameter (flags F-24, RV-01). Until an account and tag exist, this requirement is unmeetable by construction.

rows.requirement: The Site must not use an Amazon trademark or a variant of one in a domain name, subdomain, tag, or social username, and must not imply Amazon endorsement.
rows.evidence: The project name carries no Amazon mark, and this is checked rather than asserted: tools/validate_data.py::check_marks fails the build on a mark in the site name or the configured tag, and on an affirmative "endorsed by Amazon"-type claim that is not a quoted negation.

rows.requirement: The Site must not state inaccurate or misleading product claims, and may only show star ratings or reviews obtained through the Creators API or PA API.
rows.evidence: The no-guessing invariant is the repository's core design: a value is published only when an official source states it, otherwise the cell renders an explicit UNVERIFIED pill with a why-blank note (tools/build_site.py::source_cell / blank_cell), and tools/validate_data.py fails a populated product field that carries no source. No rating or review count is published anywhere; the product articles render them as "WITHHELD BY POLICY".

rows.requirement: Special Links must be qualified for search engines with rel="sponsored".
rows.evidence: Every outbound product link carries rel="sponsored nofollow" (marketing pages: rel="sponsored nofollow"; generated pages: qualified by tools/build_site.py). The CI step "Subpages disclose and never print a product price" fails any page that links to amazon.com/dp/ without rel="sponsored".

groups.name: Automation and platform capability
groups.lead: What the brief asks the platform to do automatically. Each row states the honest state of the implementation, because the brief's word "automates" and this repository's word "scaffolded" are not the same claim.

rows.requirement: Automate product research: identify candidate products and their attributes from an authorised catalog source rather than by hand.
rows.evidence: tools/amazon_creators_api.py implements the Creators API GetItems path, and tools/cache.py adds the dated snapshot layer the analysis modules read. Module M-01 is recorded as `scaffolded` in ledger/modules.json.
rows.gap: No Associates account is connected, so no live call has ever returned a catalog record in this repository. Every product attribute published here was transcribed from a manufacturer page or an Amazon product page by a session, not fetched by the automation. The automation is code-complete for the request shape and unexercised against the live API.

rows.requirement: Identify trending and high-converting products.
rows.evidence: ledger/niches.json is EMPTY_BY_DESIGN and states why: the ranking inputs require an authenticated catalog feed plus first-party click and earnings history, neither of which exists.
rows.gap: No trend, demand, or conversion figure is published anywhere in this project, and none can be until a catalog feed and a click/earnings report are connected. Publishing a shortlist now would be the exact invention the project forbids.

rows.requirement: Analyse pricing, reviews, competition and commission potential.
rows.evidence: Commission potential is fully analysed: the published rate table is transcribed in ledger/commission_table.json (11 category bands, 46 Bounty Event rows and 2 Bonus Event rows) and rendered with per-row sources. Pricing analysis is implemented as a constraint rather than a feature (R-22 forbids price tracking).
rows.gap: Review analysis (M-04) and competition assessment (M-05) are `blocked`/`scaffolded`: the reviews requirement needs a review feed obtained through the Creators API (S02), and competition needs dated SERP observations that have never been collected. Price analysis cannot be built at all in the form the brief implies, because price tracking and alerting are prohibited (RQ-03).

rows.requirement: Generate SEO-optimised product articles, comparisons and buying guides.
rows.evidence: tools/build_marketing.py + marketing/scripts/verify_marketing.py generate and gate 9 pages: a buying guide, a comparison and one article per product, each row sourced to a manufacturer page, with structured data (Product/Review with positiveNotes and negativeNotes) per S14/S15.
rows.gap: The generator is deliberately a renderer, not a writer: it fills a fixed template from verified rows and cannot produce prose. No page carries an author byline, and no page contains original observation, testing or photography — the three attributes Google's review guidance asks for first (S18). This is the direct cause of the "reads like AI slop" complaint; see the content plan.

rows.requirement: Publish and manage affiliate links and campaigns.
rows.evidence: tools/link_builder.py constructs tagged Special Links, and ledger/campaigns.json holds the campaign skeleton. Module M-08 is `scaffolded`.
rows.gap: Nothing is published through a live Associates account, and no campaign has ever run: ledger/campaigns.json holds no campaign rows. Link management is therefore tested code with no production instance.

rows.requirement: Track clicks and conversions.
rows.evidence: A first-party tracking schema exists (tools/tracking_schema.sql) and tools/redirect_server.py implements the click path. Module M-09 is `scaffolded`.
rows.gap: No click or conversion has been recorded, and none could be: the schema has no deployed database and no Associates report is connected. Tools/validate_data.py actively forbids publishing a performance field (clicks, conversion, orders, earnings) anywhere, which is why every such column in the product ledger is blank.

rows.requirement: Continuously optimise campaigns to maximise affiliate revenue.
rows.evidence: tools/optimize.py holds the optimisation loop's structure, but module M-10 is `scaffolded` and there is no campaign, no click history and no earnings report for it to optimise against.
rows.gap: This is the terminal requirement and it is the one most easily faked with a dashboard. It cannot start before RQ-10 and RQ-14 produce data, and Amazon states it makes no representation about the traffic or income an Associate can expect (compliance rule R-19), so no optimisation target can be borrowed from an official page either.

rows.requirement: Scale: run the pipeline for many products without per-product manual work.
rows.evidence: The pipeline is generator-driven: every published page is rendered from ledger JSON by tools/build_site.py and tools/build_marketing.py, and tools/validate_data.py fails the build when committed HTML drifts from the ledger. Adding a product means adding ledger rows.
rows.gap: The per-product data itself is still entered by a session from a page it read, because no catalog feed exists. Scaling the pages is solved; scaling the sourcing is not.

groups.name: Site and content quality (the "AI slop" requirement)
groups.lead: The brief's most subjective requirement, restated as things an official page actually asks for, so it can be checked instead of argued about.

rows.requirement: The site must not read as machine-generated filler: content must show effort, originality, talent or skill, and accuracy, and the role of automation must be evident to the reader.
rows.evidence: Accuracy is the strongest dimension and is genuinely enforced: every table row ends in an official-source link or an explicit blank, and the gates refuse the build otherwise. The role of automation is disclosed, which is what S40 asks for under "How".
rows.gap: Effort, originality and talent are the weak dimensions, and S40 defines them narrowly: "using generative AI to produce large amounts of text without manual oversight or curation represents little to no effort", while "writing original analysis" is the named example of high effort. The published site is mostly rendered tables plus templated sentences; there is no page where a named human states an observation, a preference, a measurement or a photograph that could only come from having handled the product.

rows.requirement: Affiliate pages must not be "thin affiliation": product descriptions and reviews may not be copied from the merchant without original content or added value.
rows.evidence: This repository is the opposite of a copy-farm on the sourcing axis: no description is copied, every specification is attributed to the manufacturer's own page, and three cross-source conflicts are published as conflicts rather than resolved silently (F-19 and the Emeril/Chefman spec conflicts). S41's named markers of value — "additional information about price, original product reviews, rigorous testing and ratings, navigation of products or categories, and product comparisons" — are met only for the last one (product comparisons).
rows.gap: Of S41's five named value markers, three are structurally unavailable here and must stay unavailable: price (prohibited, RQ-03), ratings (require a licensed feed, RQ-07), and rigorous testing (no product has been handled). That leaves original product reviews and category navigation to build. The comparison and buying guide exist and are genuinely more useful than the listing.

rows.requirement: Content must be authored and attributable; fabricated creator profiles, AI-generated headshots and made-up credentials are deception.
rows.evidence: No page in this repository carries a byline, an author page, or any statement of who produced it beyond the project name.
rows.gap: S40 states plainly that fabricating an author is deception, and S38 weighs authorship and editorial responsibility when Amazon reviews a Site. The honest options are a real named author with real credentials, or an explicit editorial statement naming the process and the reviewer — inventing an identity is the one thing that must not be done. This is a decision for the owner, so it is raised as SG-05 on the canonical decision board (editorial voice and testing) rather than guessed.

rows.requirement: Content must be current, and stale pages must be re-verified rather than left to rot.
rows.evidence: Every page prints the verification date it was built from, and the ledger carries dated snapshots (ledger/products.json verified_utc, sources.json accessed_utc), so staleness is measurable rather than invisible.
rows.gap: There is no scheduler: re-verification happens when a session runs. S38's expectation for an application review is content "generally within the last 60 days", and nothing in this repository guarantees that.

groups.name: Decision-support requirements (this request)
groups.lead: What the current request asks for, and where it now lives.

rows.requirement: A section dedicated to suggestions, where a reviewer can read proposals and choose the best path before any change is implemented.
rows.evidence: Two layers, deliberately not duplicated. The decision board itself is published at pages/suggestions.html from ledger/suggestions.json (T29 implementation session 2499438c): ten suggestions, each with two or three options, a stated recommendation, the trade-off for every option, the evidence behind it and the questions that must be answered first. This task adds the requirement layer behind it at decisions/requirements.html and the review record at decisions/flagged.html.

rows.requirement: A clear list of questions, and the information and answers that must exist before a decision can reasonably be made, including how to discover missing information.
rows.evidence: Published at pages/questions.html from ledger/questions.json (session 2499438c): sixteen questions, each stating what is already established, what is missing, how the gap can be closed, who can close it, and which suggestions it blocks. All sixteen are unanswered by design; none is filled in. This task's own generator reads the same register rather than keeping a second copy, and its hub page derives the blocker table from it.

rows.requirement: Recording the requirement set itself, so nothing in the brief is silently dropped, and so the state of each requirement is visible rather than claimed.
rows.evidence: This file. Every requirement is a row with a closed-vocabulary status and a named pointer for its evidence; tools/validate_decisions.py refuses a PARTIAL row without a gap, a MET row with a gap, or a row citing a source that does not resolve.

rows.requirement: An executive summary of the above.
rows.evidence: DECISIONS.md is the printable executive review (what is decided, what awaits a decision, what blocks it), generated from the same three ledgers as the site so the two cannot disagree. It is regenerated and drift-checked in CI.
